newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudanese opposition says kills 150 state troops.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese opposition says kills 150 state troops.

text.p: The Sudanese opposition in Cairo said their troops in eastern Sudan killed 150 government soldiers in Blue Nile province on Sunday.

"Our soldiers clashed with the government troops north of our garrison in Keili and they killed 150 of them," opposition spokesman Farouq Abu Eissa told Reuters in Cairo. Keili is 100 km (60 miles) south of Damazin, the Blue Nile capital where Sudanese troops are massing for a counterattack on the rebels.
"We also captured nine trucks, three heavy machineguns and two military vehicles," Abu Eissa added. The report could not be independently confirmed.

In a faxed statement, veteran rebel commander John Garang said that the clash, which took place between 5 a.m. and 7 a.m. local time (0300 to 0500 GMT), was proof that "the rebels can stand up to the forces of the National Islamic Front in Sudan".
"We have totally destroyed the 'Torrential Flood' troops of the army," it added. Torrential Flood is an army codename.
The opposition says it has seized several towns and garrisons in the Blue Nile area but the government only admits to the loss of Kurmuk and Qeissan near the Ethiopian border.

The rebels say their goal is to advance on Damazin, site of a hydroelectricity plant which supplies Khartoum with most its power, to put pressure on the Sudanese government and bring about a popular uprising.
Sudan says neighbours Eritrean and Ethiopian troops are doing the fighting and that the rebel troops are nothing but mercenaries. Both states, and also Egypt, deny these charges.
